passages.text: After Rehoboam had established his sovereignty and royal power, he and all Israel with him forsook the Law of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was king of Judah.
He established his kingdom.
He became strong as king.
Rehoboam abandoned the Law of the LORD.
All Israel abandoned the Law of the LORD with him.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כְּהָכִ֞ין מַלְכ֤וּת רְחַבְעָם֙ וּכְחֶזְקָת֔וֹ עָזַ֖ב אֶת־ תּוֹרַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִמּֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, because they had been unfaithful to the LORD, Shishak king of Egypt came up and attacked Jerusalem with 1,200 chariots, 60,000 horsemen, and countless troops who came with him out of Egypt—Libyans, Sukkites, and Cushites.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was king in Jerusalem.
He ruled for five years.
The people of Judah and Israel were unfaithful to the LORD.
Shishak was king of Egypt.
Shishak came up against Jerusalem.
He brought 1,200 chariots.
He brought 60,000 horsemen.
He brought many troops from Egypt.
No one could count all the people who came with him.
Libyans came with Shishak.
Sukkites came with Shishak.
Cushites came with Shishak.
Shishak attacked Jerusalem because the people had turned away from the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הַֽחֲמִישִׁית֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֔ם עָלָ֛ה שִׁישַׁ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֥י מָעֲל֖וּ בַּיהוָֽה׃ בְּאֶ֤לֶף וּמָאתַ֙יִם֙ רֶ֔כֶב וּבְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֗ר לָעָ֞ם אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֤אוּ עִמּוֹ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לוּבִ֥ים סֻכִּיִּ֖ים וְכוּשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: He captured the fortified cities of Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Shishak was the king of Egypt.
Shishak attacked Judah.
Shishak captured the fortified cities of Judah.
Shishak came as far as Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיִּלְכֹּ֛ד אֶת־ עָרֵ֥י הַמְּצֻר֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֖א עַד־ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah who had gathered at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and he said to them, “This is what the LORD says: ‘You have forsaken Me; therefore, I have forsaken you into the hand of Shishak.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Shemaiah was a prophet.
Rehoboam was the king of Judah.
The leaders of Judah had gathered at Jerusalem.
They gathered because Shishak, king of Egypt, attacked.
Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders.
Shemaiah spoke to them.
He said, “This is what the LORD says.
You have forsaken Me.
Therefore, I have forsaken you.
I have given you into the hand of Shishak.”
passages.original: וּֽשְׁמַֽעְיָ֤ה הַנָּבִיא֙ בָּ֣א אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֔ם וְשָׂרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ נֶאֶסְפ֥וּ אֶל־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מִפְּנֵ֣י שִׁישָׁ֑ק וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם כֹּה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַתֶּם֙ עֲזַבְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִ֔י וְאַף־ אֲנִ֛י עָזַ֥בְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּיַד־ שִׁישָֽׁק׃

passages.text: So the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, “The LORD is righteous.”
passages.sermon: The leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves.\r\nThey said, “The LORD is righteous.”
passages.original: וַיִּכָּנְע֥וּ שָׂרֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְהַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ צַדִּ֥יק׀ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, saying, “They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them, but will soon grant them deliverance. My wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.
passages.sermon:
The LORD saw that the people humbled themselves.
The LORD spoke to Shemaiah the prophet.
The LORD said, “They have humbled themselves.
I will not destroy them.
I will give them a little deliverance.
I will not pour out my wrath on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.”
passages.original: וּבִרְא֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ כִּ֣י נִכְנָ֔עוּ הָיָה֩ דְבַר־ יְהוָ֨ה אֶל־ שְׁמַֽעְיָ֧ה׀ לֵאמֹ֛ר נִכְנְע֖וּ לֹ֣א אַשְׁחִיתֵ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֨י לָהֶ֤ם כִּמְעַט֙ לִפְלֵיטָ֔ה וְלֹא־ תִתַּ֧ךְ חֲמָתִ֛י בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּיַד־ שִׁישָֽׁק׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, they will become his servants, so that they may learn the difference between serving Me and serving the kings of other lands.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke about the people of Israel.
God said they will become servants to another king.
God wanted them to learn something important.
God wanted them to know what it means to serve Him.
God also wanted them to know what it means to serve the kings of other nations.
God wanted them to see the difference between serving Him and serving other rulers.
passages.original: כִּ֥י יִהְיוּ־ ל֖וֹ לַעֲבָדִ֑ים וְיֵדְעוּ֙ עֲב֣וֹדָתִ֔י וַעֲבוֹדַ֖ת מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאֲרָצֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: So King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem and seized the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the royal palace. He took everything, including the gold shields that Solomon had made.
passages.sermon:
King Shishak ruled Egypt.
King Shishak attacked Jerusalem.
He took the treasures from the house of the LORD.
He took the treasures from the royal palace.
He took everything.
He took the gold shields.
Solomon had made these gold shields.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַל שִׁישַׁ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַיִם֮ עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִַם֒ וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־ אֹצְר֣וֹת בֵּית־ יְהוָ֗ה וְאֶת־ אֹֽצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֶת־ הַכֹּ֖ל לָקָ֑ח וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־ מָגִנֵּ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

passages.text: Then King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and committed them to the care of the captains of the guard on duty at the entrance to the royal palace.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam ruled in Jerusalem.
King Rehoboam lost the gold shields that Solomon had made.
King Shishak of Egypt took the gold shields when he attacked Jerusalem.
King Rehoboam made new shields from bronze to replace the gold ones.
King Rehoboam gave the bronze shields to the captains of the guard.
The captains of the guard watched over the entrance to the royal palace.
The captains kept the bronze shields at the palace entrance.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ רְחַבְעָם֙ תַּחְתֵּיהֶ֔ם מָגִנֵּ֖י נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְהִפְקִ֗יד עַל־ יַד֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרָצִ֔ים הַשֹּׁ֣מְרִ֔ים פֶּ֖תַח בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: And whenever the king entered the house of the LORD, the guards would go with him, bearing the shields, and later they would return them to the guardroom.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam ruled in Jerusalem.
Whenever King Rehoboam entered the house of the LORD, the guards went with him.
The guards carried the bronze shields.
Afterward, the guards returned the shields to the guardroom.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֛י מִדֵּי־ ב֥וֹא הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה בָּ֤אוּ הָרָצִים֙ וּנְשָׂא֔וּם וֶהֱשִׁב֖וּם אֶל־ תָּ֥א הָרָצִֽים׃

passages.text: Because Rehoboam humbled himself, the anger of the LORD turned away from him, and He did not destroy him completely. Indeed, conditions were good in Judah.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was king of Judah.
Rehoboam humbled himself before God.
The LORD turned His anger away from Rehoboam.
The LORD did not destroy Rehoboam completely.
There were good things in Judah.
passages.original: וּבְהִכָּֽנְע֗וֹ שָׁ֤ב מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ אַף־ יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א לְהַשְׁחִ֖ית לְכָלָ֑ה וְגַם֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה הָיָ֖ה דְּבָרִ֥ים טוֹבִֽים׃ס

passages.text: Thus King Rehoboam established himself in Jerusalem. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel in which to put His Name. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam ruled in Jerusalem.
He became strong as king there.
Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to rule.
He ruled for seventeen years in Jerusalem.
The LORD chose Jerusalem from all the tribes of Israel.
The LORD put His Name in Jerusalem.
Rehoboam’s mother was Naamah.
Naamah was an Ammonite.
passages.original: וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֞ק הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֛ם בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיִּמְלֹ֑ךְ כִּ֣י בֶן־ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים וְאַחַ֣ת שָׁנָה֩ רְחַבְעָ֨ם בְּמָלְכ֜וֹ וּֽשֲׁבַ֨ע עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֣ה׀ מָלַ֣ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הָ֠עִיר אֲשֶׁר־ בָּחַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לָשׂ֨וּם אֶת־ שְׁמ֥וֹ שָׁם֙ מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ נַעֲמָ֖ה הָֽעַמֹּנִֽית׃

passages.text: And Rehoboam did evil because he did not set his heart to seek the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was king of Judah.
Rehoboam did evil.
He did not set his heart to seek the LORD.
This was the reason for his evil actions.
passages.original: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ הָרָ֑ע כִּ֣י לֹ֤א הֵכִין֙ לִבּ֔וֹ לִדְר֖וֹשׁ אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Now the acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the Prophet and of Iddo the Seer concerning the genealogies? There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their days.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was a king of Judah.
Shemaiah was a prophet.
Iddo was a seer.
The records of Shemaiah and Iddo contain the acts of Rehoboam.
These records include the first acts and the last acts of Rehoboam.
The records also include the genealogies.
Rehoboam and Jeroboam fought wars against each other.
They were at war all their days.
passages.original: וְדִבְרֵ֣י רְחַבְעָ֗ם הָרִאשֹׁנִים֙ וְהָאֲ֣חַרוֹנִ֔ים הֲלֹא־ הֵ֨ם כְּתוּבִ֜ים בְּדִבְרֵ֨י שְׁמַֽעְיָ֧ה הַנָּבִ֛יא וְעִדּ֥וֹ הַחֹזֶ֖ה לְהִתְיַחֵ֑שׂ וּמִלְחֲמ֧וֹת רְחַבְעָ֛ם וְיָרָבְעָ֖ם כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: And Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And his son Abijah reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam died.
People buried Rehoboam in the City of David.
Abijah was Rehoboam’s son.
Abijah became king after Rehoboam.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב רְחַבְעָם֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲבִיָּ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
